title.value: MixEHR-Guided: A guided multi-modal topic modeling approach for large-scale automatic phenotyping using the electronic health record
title.justification: This title accurately reflects the content and focus of the paper, which discusses the development and application of a novel model, MixEHR-G, for automatic phenotyping using electronic health records (EHR).
title.quote: MixEHR-Guided: A guided multi-modal topic modeling approach for large-scale automatic phenotyping using the electronic health record

extractions.description: The paper presents MixEHR-G, a multi-modal topic modeling approach designed to improve automatic phenotyping in electronic health records (EHR). This method utilizes prior information from surrogate features to align topics with known phenotypes, enhancing the interpretability and accuracy of phenotyping without the need for extensive expert input. The model is applied to EHR datasets, such as MIMIC-III and PopHR, demonstrating its capability to generate clinically meaningful phenotype topics useful for clinical research and epidemiological analysis. The approach significantly improves over previous methods in terms of accuracy and scalability, facilitating applications in digital medicine and public health.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is not directly related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. The primary focus is on improving automatic phenotyping using electronic health records for clinical and translational research.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Electronic Health Records (EHRs) offer high volume comprehensive observational patient health data for clinical and translational research.

primary_category.justification: The paper's focus is on biomedical informatics and the development of computational models for healthcare applications, which do not align with climate or ecological sustainable development themes.
primary_category.quote: We present a novel automatic phenotyping model called MixEHR-Guided (MixEHR-G), a multimodal hierarchical Bayesian topic model that efficiently models the EHR generative process by identifying latent phenotype structure in the data.

primary_sub_category.justification: There are no sub-categories within Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development that match the focus on electronic health record phenotyping.
primary_sub_category.quote: This process is tedious and error-prone due to recall and observer biases in how codes and measures are selected, and some phenotypes are incompletely captured by a handful of surrogate features.

applications.value: Automatic phenotyping in healthcare using EHR data
applications.justification: This application is repeatedly emphasized throughout the paper as the primary use case for the developed MixEHR-G model.
applications.quote: MixEHR-G outperforms existing unsupervised phenotyping methods on a phenotype label annotation task, and it can accurately estimate relative phenotype prevalence functions without gold-standard phenotype information.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper is not related to any category under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_category.quote: Altogether, MixEHR-G is an important step towards building an interpretable and automated phenotyping system using EHR data.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: No new sub-category can be suggested that relates this work to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Unlike existing topic modeling algorithms wherein the inferred topics are not identifiable, MixEHR-G uses prior information from informative surrogate features to align topics with known phenotypes.
